gates.reason: Security permissions and egress/boundary checks are present, but mutable action tags allow upstream code substitution.
Inspected the configured parser, cache-parity, provenance, and recommendation-contract gates; no workflow-level integrity defect found.
The workflow enforces server/SPA bundle budgets, cold-path dependency isolation, cache behavior, dataset reuse, and performance-probe logic.
The PR workflow has read-only repository permission, but its checkout and Node setup actions use mutable major-version tags.
This workflow measures browser loading performance and defines no detector, parser, recommendation claim, or validated fix snippet.
Both published flavors are built and measured with cold-load FCP, interactivity, content-painted, and CLS budgets.

The generated doc-time provenance is based on full Git history and the packaged manifest is checked for schema, completeness, and exact commit binding.
This is release image publication orchestration, not application hot-path code or a new runtime surface requiring a latency/bundle probe.

findings.title: Mutable GitHub Action tags permit supply-chain code substitution
findings.what: These workflows invoke actions/checkout, actions/setup-node, and actions/upload-artifact through mutable major-version tags. If an upstream tag is moved or its publishing account is compromised, substituted action code executes on self-hosted runners. In docker-publish.yml that code runs in a job granted packages:write and receives the GHCR token, enabling image/package compromise.
findings.fix: Replace every tag-based `uses:` reference with the action release's reviewed full 40-character commit SHA, retaining the release version in a comment; keep the already SHA-pinned Docker actions unchanged.
findings.acceptance: A deterministic workflow scan finds that every external `uses:` reference in these three files ends in `@` followed by exactly 40 hexadecimal characters, and the publishing workflow still grants packages:write only to its publish job.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the cited baseline lines at c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The mutable references remain present across all three files; by comparison, docker-publish.yml:88,96,187,225,255 already demonstrates the intended immutable-SHA pattern. The claim is limited to executable action references and does not depend on repository narrative.
